newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foghorns summon Russian Far East to protest.
newsitem.headline: Foghorns summon Russian Far East to protest.

text.p: Merchant seamen in the Russian Far East led the nation's workers into a day of protest on Tuesday against unpaid wages and broken government promises, blasting their foghorns in Vladivostok harbour.
Trade unions representing millions of public and private sector employees, many not paid for months, have called for strikes and demonstrations across the country.

More than 20,000 people in Russia's main Pacific port marched to Vladivostok's main square to hear labour leaders rail against local politicians, the government and President Boris Yeltsin -- who, by coincidence, was undergoing heart surgery.
A union resolution in Vladivostok accused the government of running a "destructive social economic policy".

Across the thinly-populated eastern Primorsky region, which overwhelmingly backed Yeltsin's reelection in July, some 160,000 workers turned out for protests and meetings, unions estimated. No official figure was immediately available.
Union leaders say unpaid wages in October stood at some 42.8 trillion roubles (nearly $8 billion) nationwide. Government figures, available only for September, put the arrears at 40 trillion roubles.

In a move that appeared designed to soothe tempers, Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Ignatenko told Itar-Tass news agency that Chernomyrdin, who is acting head of state during Yeltsin;s operations, had ordered the government to bring forward and increase budgeted payments for health, education and culture.
But that will not help the millions of private sector workers, military personnel and others who have not been paid.
